newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai Dazhong sees net up 9.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai Dazhong sees net up 9.1 pct.

text.p: Shanghai Dazhong Taxi expects net profits of 110 million yuan in 1996, up 9.1 percent from 100.8 million yuan in 1995, a company official said on Monday.

The official told a news briefing that the firm, the biggest taxi company in Shanghai, was planning a major expansion into other cities around China over the next few years, and planned to expand its fleet of 2,000 taxis to 10,000 by the year 2000.
This would make it the world's biggest taxi company, the official said.
By the year 2000, the firm was aiming to raise annual net profits to 200 million yuan, he added.
The company posted net profits of 55.954 million yuan in the first half of 1996, up from 51.832 million yuan in the same 1995 period. ($1 = 8.3 yuan)
